title: openai/math cross-reference index
scope: Results from openai/math that BPR has considered, pinned to one upstream commit. Every entry is context only: no unification-map node's status or limitation depends on any entry, and the map loader never reads this file. Bookkeeping, not a validity check of any upstream result.
bottom_line: No openai/math result changes the status or limitation of any unification-map node.

upstream.name: openai/math
upstream.author: OpenAI
upstream.upstream_disclaimer: Paraphrase of the upstream README: results are at different stages of verification, not all have Lean formalizations, and some unformalized results could have issues.

vocab_notes.verification: Describes the statement in statement_bpr, not the family: lean_main_statement means that statement is a Lean comparator statement (its scope recorded in lean_scope_excerpt); lean_supporting_only means a comparator exists but covers only supporting results; manuscript_only means no comparator covers it.
vocab_notes.verification_source: formalization_yaml: the comparator is listed in lean/formalization.yaml main_results; lean_docs_only: it is linked only from lean/docs/<family>.md.
vocab_notes.bpr_check: none: BPR has not checked the comparator against the manuscript; statement_read: a BPR reviewer read the comparator statement against the manuscript (fidelity_check records it); built: the comparator was re-run by BPR in an isolated sandbox.
vocab_notes.usage_cap: rigorous_input requires lean_main_statement, bpr_check built, a fidelity check, an active upstream status and no external dependencies; nothing in this index is above context_only.
vocab_notes.review_verdict: survived_value_refuted: passed the hypotheses and reliability lenses, rejected as a substantive integration; context_only_unverified: single-agent triage, not adversarially verified; considered_not_cited: used by no BPR argument and cited nowhere.

entries.family_title: Unique Games and optimal approximation thresholds
entries.title: A Direct Proof of Optimal Max-Cut Hardness
entries.result_ref: Main theorem (TeX label thm:main); Lean comparator OAI.OptimalMaxCut.main
entries.statement_bpr: For every fixed alpha with alpha_GW < alpha <= 1, where alpha_GW = min over -1 <= rho < 1 of 2 arccos(rho) / (pi (1 - rho)) = 0.8785672..., there is a deterministic polynomial-time reduction (a Mathlib TM2 machine with finite tape alphabets) from binary-encoded 3SAT to finite simple unweighted graphs with a positive integer scale Q and rationals yesBound > 0, noBound >= 0, noBound < alpha * yesBound: satisfiable inputs give maxCut/Q >= yesBound and unsatisfiable inputs give maxCut/Q <= noBound.
not_covered: The step from this reduction to 'NP-hard' (Cook-Levin) and the algorithmic corollary (no fixed ratio above alpha_GW unless P = NP; NP not in BPP for guarantees in expectation): informal, not in Lean
Ratios alpha_GW + o(1)
Average-case instances such as G(n, 1/2); dense graphs admit a PTAS
Any fixed n, including the n <= 14 and n = 500 claims in bpr/optimization.py
The manuscript's direct proof: the Lean proof goes through the formalized Unique Games theorem plus a KKMO-type gadget, so Lean certifies the statement, not the paper's argument
P versus NP itself
entries.lean_scope_excerpt: Max-Cut paragraph of lean/docs/102.md: for every fixed alpha with alpha_GW < alpha <= 1, a deterministic polynomial-time reduction from binary 3SAT to a strictly separated Max-Cut gap on finite simple unweighted graphs, with an explicit positive integer scale as part of the output. The same page also scopes the Unique Games, Vertex Cover, Min-UnCut and directed feedback vertex set statements; its sentence that no P != NP assumption is built in belongs to the Vertex Cover paragraph (for Max-Cut, read the comparator).

fidelity_check.by: BPR review (deep review and hypotheses lens), re-read while indexing
fidelity_check.note: Comparator MainStatement read against the manuscript's main theorem, the gap theorem and the unweighted lemma: it matches. Not built. The Lean kernel and Mathlib's TM2ComputableInPolyTime at the pinned Mathlib revision are trusted, not checked.

classical_fallback: Håstad 2001 with Trevisan–Sorkin–Sudan–Williamson 2000: approximating Max-Cut beyond 16/17 is NP-hard (unconditional)
Khot–Kindler–Mossel–O'Donnell 2007 with Mossel–O'Donnell–Oleszkiewicz 2010: alpha_GW is optimal assuming the Unique Games Conjecture
Goemans–Williamson 1995: the alpha_GW approximation algorithm
entries.bpr_usage: At most one worst-case context line in the MaxCutBPR STATUS block. Not a reason for withdrawing the old MaxCutBPR claims, no docstring tripwire, no note in bpr/complexity.py.

review.note: Worst-case asymptotic ceiling on claims BPR never makes (fixed n, G(n, 1/2)); changes no decision. The MaxCutBPR sign error and the broken Bridge 9 call were found while scoping this citation; they are BPR-internal findings and are not credited to openai/math.

entries.family_title: Gaussian free field limits for the balanced six-vertex model
entries.title: The Gaussian free field limit of the balanced six-vertex model with variance multiplier 1/arcsin(c/2)
entries.result_ref: Main theorem (TeX label thm:main)
entries.statement_bpr: Six-vertex model on Z^2 with weights a = b = 1 and c in (0, 2], in the zero-slope plane state P_c defined as an iterated local limit of column-balanced tori (first M -> infinity, then even L -> infinity): the rescaled height function converges to sigma(c) times the plane Gaussian free field modulo constants (Green function -(1/2 pi) log|x - y|), with sigma(c)^2 = 1/arcsin(c/2). Pairings with neutral finite-energy measures converge jointly to Gaussians, and mixed moments of distinct point increments with pairwise disjoint endpoints converge. At c = 1 (square ice): sigma^2 = 6/pi and the height variogram is (6/pi^2) log r + O(1).
not_covered: Uniqueness among Gibbs states, other slopes or flux sectors, and estimates uniform as c -> 0
Lattice-scale (single-link) correlations; a single sharp flux has logarithmically divergent variance, so 'fluxes jointly Gaussian with covariance (3/2 pi) C_ij' is false as stated
Equivalence between BPR's finite zero-flux tori and P_1 (not proved by BPR)
Any 3D statement: emergent_gauge_field is a 3D claim, and the 2D RK point is the z = 2 point where BPR's photon speed vanishes and 2+1D compact U(1) confines away from it
external_dependencies: DKLM2026 (arXiv:2603.06268) Thms 4.3-4.4 and its zero-slope equilibrium characterization: needed at c = 1 for the identification of P_1 and the value of the multiplier. c = 1 lies outside that paper's own main-theorem range (sqrt(3) <= c <= 2) and rests on its stated extension to 1 <= c <= 2. Not checked by BPR.
Lammers–Tassy strict convexity of the surface tension (c >= 1), as cited by the preprint. Not checked by BPR.
The preprint's own normalization section covers c < 1 only.
classical_fallback: Di Francesco–Saleur–Zuber 1987: the same variance as a Coulomb-gas prediction (square-ice stiffness K = pi/6), non-rigorous; cite it first
Lieb 1967: exact residual entropy of square ice, an independent refereed known answer
entries.bpr_usage: Considered, tangential. No section 6a, no sampler or GFF helpers, no demonstration_report reference, no map revision and no Monte Carlo test against 6/pi.

review.note: Analogue only; nothing in BPR consumes it. The 4x4 link-boson torus findings (2970/990/69/1) are BPR-internal and not credited to openai/math.

entries.family_title: Positive-temperature Bose–Einstein condensation and exact quantum depletion
entries.title: Ground-state condensation in the dilute hard-sphere gas
entries.result_ref: Main theorem 'Condensation in every ground state' (TeX label main:theorem); Lean comparator OAI.HardSphere.condensation_with_mixed
entries.statement_bpr: For the continuum hard-sphere Bose gas (sphere radius a) on large tori there are absolute constants eps_0, c_0 > 0 such that, whenever rho a^3 < eps_0, every ground state (pure, or mixed and supported on the ground space) has condensate fraction with liminf >= c_0 along every thermodynamic sequence N/L^3 -> rho.
not_covered: Positive-temperature BEC and quantum depletion, the family headline: paper-only, in the 2026-10-05 companions
Lattice bosons, including BPR's cubic Bose-Hubbard model and its free continuum limit (zero scattering length at g >= 0)
Fixed g at arbitrary density (a small gas parameter is required)
Any phonon-branch statement
entries.lean_scope_excerpt: lean/docs/267.md: ground-state Bose-Einstein condensation in the dilute hard-sphere gas; absolute constants eps_0, c_0 > 0 such that if rho a^3 < eps_0 the condensate fraction has liminf >= c_0 along every thermodynamic sequence N/L^3 -> rho; covers every pure ground state, mixed states supported on the ground space and the ground-space projection; no positive-temperature assertion. The comparator is not in lean/formalization.yaml main_results.
classical_fallback: Dyson–Lieb–Simon 1978 (J. Stat. Phys. 18) and Kennedy–Lieb–Shastry 1988: long-range order via reflection positivity in special lattice cases (e.g. hard-core bosons at half filling), which is what the thermodynamic_condensation limitation already cites
Lieb–Seiringer 2002 (Phys. Rev. Lett. 88): BEC for dilute trapped gases in the Gross–Pitaevskii limit, not the thermodynamic limit
entries.bpr_usage: Context next to the thermodynamic_condensation open problem in the condensate note. Not the basis for any wording change to that node: such changes must rest on refereed sources (Dyson–Lieb–Simon, Kennedy–Lieb–Shastry, Capogrosso-Sansone et al. 2007).

review.note: Deep single-agent review: not applicable as an input (continuum, small gas parameter, no phonon theorem). Triaged by a single agent and not adversarially verified; read the source theorem before citing.

entries.statement_bpr: Nearest-neighbour isotropic quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet on Z^d with d >= 3 and any spin S in {1/2, 1, 3/2, ...}: for every sufficiently large beta there is a translation-invariant beta-KMS state (zero-field dynamics) with magnetization <S_0^z> >= S/4.

A hard-core-boson reading (off-diagonal long-range order for hard-core bosons with nearest-neighbour attraction at the tuned SU(2) point): not part of the Lean statement
BPR's model: BPR has no nearest-neighbour attraction, and the gapless mode here is a quadratic magnon, not a phonon
entries.lean_scope_excerpt: lean/docs/271.md: spontaneous magnetization for the nearest-neighbour isotropic quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet on Z^d for every d >= 3 and every spin S; at every sufficiently low positive temperature a translation-invariant KMS state for the zero-field dynamics with magnetization at least S/4; also convergence of the finite-volume dynamics. entries.family_title: The Benjamini–Schramm nonuniqueness conjecture
entries.title: Nonuniqueness of percolation on nonamenable quasi-transitive graphs
entries.result_ref: Corollary 'Critical laws and exponential connectivity' (TeX label cor:critical-laws); Lean comparator OAI.Percolation.BenjaminiSchramm.critical_laws. The paper's headline is the nonuniqueness theorem (TeX label thm:main)
entries.statement_bpr: Bernoulli bond percolation on every infinite connected locally finite nonamenable quasi-transitive graph has mean-field critical behaviour: a finite triangle diagram at p_c, susceptibility of order (p_c - p)^(-1) as p increases to p_c, and percolation probability of order p - p_c as p decreases to p_c.

entries.family_title: GOE bulk universality for regular graphs with weak Anderson disorder
entries.title: GOE bulk universality for fixed-degree random regular graphs
entries.result_ref: Main theorem (TeX label thm:main)
entries.statement_bpr: For every fixed degree d >= 3 and fixed energy E in (-2 sqrt(d-1), 2 sqrt(d-1)), the eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix of a uniformly random simple d-regular graph on n vertices, centred at E and unfolded by n times the Kesten-McKay density at E, have local statistics converging (Laplace functionals of nonnegative compactly supported test functions) to those of the GOE bulk as n -> infinity.

Weighted or disordered graphs (the weak-Anderson-disorder companion is a separate unformalized preprint)

Bauerschmidt–Huang–Knowles–Yau 2017 (Ann. Probab. 45): bulk GOE statistics when the degree grows between N^eps and N^(2/3 - eps)
Kesten 1959; McKay 1981: the limiting spectral density

entries.family_title: QAOA attains the SK optimum in the thermodynamic-first limit
entries.title: QAOA attains the SK ground-state energy in the thermodynamic-first limit
entries.result_ref: Main theorem (TeX label thm:main) and Corollary 'Regular MaxCut in successive limits' (TeX label cor:regular-maxcut)
entries.statement_bpr: For the zero-field SK model the optimal depth-p QAOA value tends to the Parisi ground-state constant P* as p -> infinity (system size first). Corollary: for every eta > 0 a fixed-depth QAOA word gives cut fraction >= 1/2 + (P* - eta)/sqrt(D) on every (D+1)-regular graph of large enough girth, for D >= D_0.
not_covered: QAOA convergence itself is not formalized; the Lean statements are conditional on an admissible Parisi minimizer
Finite n or finite D; the limits are successive (n first, then p or D)
Any statement about BPR's phase-oscillator solver

Variational identities for the zero-field SK ground-state energy used in the paper's argument, conditional on an admissible Parisi minimizer and its diffusion (convergence of the finite-system ground-state energy to the Parisi value; martingale and curvature formulas; finite Gaussian approximation); the selected statement does not assert convergence of the circuit energies. A second comparator (another manuscript) proves full support of zero-temperature Parisi minimizers on [0, 1).

entries.family_title: The optimal quartic separation between randomized and quantum queries
entries.title: A Nearly Quartic Separation Between Randomized and Quantum Query Complexity
entries.result_ref: Main theorem (TeX label thm:main)
entries.statement_bpr: For total Boolean functions the optimal power relating randomized and quantum query complexity is 4: R(f) = O((1 + Q(f))^4) (prior literature), and for each fixed k >= 2 there are total functions with Q = O(sqrt(m) polylog m) and R = Omega(m^(2 - 1/k) / log^2 m), so no smaller exponent works.
not_covered: Partial functions and promise problems, where exponential separations exist
Time complexity or physical parallelism; this is query complexity only
classical_fallback: Beals–Buhrman–Cleve–Mosca–de Wolf 2001 (J. ACM 48): D(f) = O(Q(f)^6) for total functions, already enough for the caveat that quantum speedups for total functions are polynomially bounded
Aaronson–Ben-David–Kothari–Rao–Tal 2021 (STOC): R(f) = O(Q(f)^4)
entries.bpr_usage: Caveat for TopologicalParallelism: quantum query speedups for total functions are polynomially bounded; cite the classical bounds first, the matching lower bound only as unrefereed context.

review.note: Triaged by a single agent and not adversarially verified; read the source theorem before citing.

entries.family_title: Approximate counting and entropy of perfect matchings
entries.title: A Fully Polynomial Randomized Approximation Scheme for Perfect Matchings in General Graphs
entries.result_ref: Main theorem (TeX label thm:main); Lean comparator OAI.MatchingFPRAS.thm_main
entries.statement_bpr: There is a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for counting perfect matchings of every finite simple undirected graph: relative error eps with probability >= 1 - delta, output zero when there is no perfect matching, worst-case running time polynomial in the input length, 1/eps and log(1/delta).
not_covered: The companion entropy paper's sharp face-dimension bound (outside its Lean statement)
Any claim about BPR's ice manifold: reading P_0 as f-factors (each corresponds to prod_v (d_v - q_v)! perfect matchings via Tutte's gadget) is BPR's own observation, and no BPR claim depends on |P_0|
The RK ground state of a single flip class (the uniform measure on all of P_0 is a different object)
entries.lean_scope_excerpt: lean/docs/113.md: a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for counting perfect matchings in every finite simple undirected graph (relative error eps with probability >= 1 - delta, zero output when none exists, polynomial worst-case time); also the perfect-matching entropy bounds and deterministic approximations; the paper's sharp global face-dimension bound is outside the selected statements. The FPRAS comparator is not in lean/formalization.yaml main_results.
